reviews.one_line_contribution: A controlled dose-response study on agent traces (ALFWorld/WebShop) that decomposes injected-experience harm into token load, item count, and the number of injected items whose recommended action is off the expert plan, claims the harm is a step function of the third with a knee at the first wrong item, and concludes that a swept static k plus wrong-item removal can replace a learned retrieval budget.
reviews.closest_prior_work: VERIFIED: arXiv:2605.10828, 'The First Drop of Ink: Nonlinear Impact of Misleading Information in Long-Context Reasoning' (2026-05-11; confirmed by direct s2cli `paper` lookup and independently returned by my recency-restricted mechanism query). This is the real threat and the proposal concedes it: the mechanism claim -- degradation is a sharply nonlinear function of the count of misleading items rather than of length, with most of the drop at the first slice of distractors -- is already published across three model families. What is left is the substrate (tool-use traces instead of 128K multi-document QA), the automatic wrong-action label from expert plans, and the budget-rule corollary: a domain-transfer replication with better controls, not a new phenomenon. It is squeezed from the other side by arXiv:2608.03297 (Distractor-Aware Truncation, verified 2026-08-04), which already concludes that any context-length study must specify how it separates signal from distractor or be ambiguous between exactly the two hypotheses this proposal pits against each other, and by arXiv:2510.05381 (verified: 'Context Length Alone Hurts LLM Performance Despite Perfect Retrieval', EMNLP, 150 citations), which establishes the opposing pure-length effect the proposal predicts it will not see. Second-closest verified: arXiv:2505.00234 (Self-Generated In-Context Examples, NeurIPS 2025, 19 citations), correctly characterized as the nearest k-selection neighbour with no dose decomposition; arXiv:2607.13591 (MemCon, verified) is the learned-budget comparator; arXiv:2605.09330 (Trap of Trajectory / CAMEL, verified) calibrates reliance on spurious trajectory patterns without sweeping wrong-item counts, so it is related work rather than a collision.
reviews.strongest_objection: Three objections compound. (1) The pivotal falsifier is set in a regime where it cannot fail. P1 says the proposal is dead if length-matched padding reproduces half the top-15 harm, but the padding arm spans roughly 1.5-5K tokens, while the verified length-alone effect (2510.05381) and the nonlinearity it is testing against (2605.10828) are both measured at ~128K. A null on P1 is close to guaranteed by the choice of token range, so passing it is uninformative about the general claim in the title; only the head-to-head against the program's own memory_budget_confound, which lives in the same small regime, survives. (2) The remaining predictions are ratios of an effect whose absolute size sits at or below the detection floor. The pilot harm is a handful of flipped items out of a few hundred tasks and the quoted MDE is ~3 points on ~2,000 paired episodes per cell; P2 ('one wrong item gives at least 60 percent of the harm of four') and P3 ('one rank-7 wrong item reproduces at least half of the k=7 harm') require separating 0.6H from 0.35H, which needs several times the power quoted for detecting H at all. The plan computes an MDE only on the level, never on the contrast or on the knee-versus-linear model comparison, so the likely outcome is intervals compatible with both models -- not the pre-registered ruling it promises. (3) The scalar dose variable in the title is not well defined by the proposal's own predictions: P4 asserts that relevance-matched wrong items harm more than random-task wrong items at matched tokens, yet both are wrong-action items under the paper's automatic label. If P4 holds, harm depends on how many items are wrong *and* how close they are, a two-parameter retriever-dependent quantity, and 'not how many, but how many are wrong' degrades to 'how many are wrong and similar', which no longer cleanly displaces the count hypothesis.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: First, put the pure-length arm where the competing hypothesis actually lives: either extend padding into the regime where 2510.05381 measures a length-alone effect, or restate P1 explicitly as a claim about the few-thousand-token memory budget only, and drop 'not token load' from the title's generality. Second, re-power on the contrast rather than the level: pre-register an MDE for the j=1-versus-j=4 difference and for the knee-versus-linear AIC gap, and choose a confirmatory regime where total harm at k=15 is large enough for a 60/40 split to resolve -- the weakest backbone and the hardest ALFWorld task types, not the 27B -- reporting achieved discordance counts against the null-replicate floor before committing to the full grid. Third, make the label defensible: ALFWorld admits multiple valid plans, so 'off the single expert plan' is not 'wrong'. Use plan-equivalence or an environment rollout of the item's recommended first action, and report the disagreement rate against the expert-plan rule in the 200-item audit, since mislabelling lands squarely on the organically retrieved top-k arms where the load-bearing P3 reconstruction sits. Fourth, close the oracle gap with a realizable wrong-item detector (retrieval-score threshold, agreement between the item's recommended first action and the agent's memory-free first action, or a local verifier) and report the static-k rule under it; oracle filtering is a ceiling, not a method. Fifth, pre-register whether the dose variable is a raw or similarity-weighted count so P4 cannot silently rewrite the thesis. Sixth, cut scope: three backbones x three positions x two granularities x two padding types plus a bandit is exploratory breadth presented as a plan, and the confirmatory core alone runs to tens of thousands of ALFWorld episodes on one 4xA100 node that must also serve a 120B MoE.
reviews.missing_baseline: A non-oracle, implementable read-time filter -- most obviously a retrieval-score / similarity-threshold cutoff (drop items below score s, letting k vary per task), and secondarily a self-consistency or verifier filter that flags an item whose recommended first action disagrees with the agent's memory-free first action. The plan has 'oracle-filtered injection at k=15' as its ceiling and 'no memory / top-k / 2505.00234-style selection / MemCon bandit' as floor and comparator, with nothing between them. This is the baseline that decides whether the paper has a deliverable: the advertised contribution is 'a static rule for setting the injection budget', but the rule requires counting items whose action is off the expert plan -- precisely the quantity unavailable at inference time. Without a realizable filter the headline collapses to 'if you could already identify the misleading items, removing them would help', and a plain similarity threshold might capture most of the oracle's benefit, deflating the contribution entirely. Secondary omission: no per-task adaptive-k-by-retrieval-score-mass baseline, which is the practical alternative the learned-budget papers are actually competing against.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision found. The proposal's own check is well above average for this program -- it names channels, separates premise citations from prior-work claims, flags arXiv:2609.01556 as unverifiable on S2/HF, and correctly demotes 2605.09330 from collision to related work -- and I credit it. Every query below ran on channel (a), the s2cli command; WebSearch and WebFetch are unavailable in this session, so channel (b) answered nothing. (1) 'dose-response of injected experience items agent trajectories how many retrieved memories harm' -> InjecMEM 2608.23471, The Compliance Trap 2607.10608, MemSyco-Bench 2607.01071, LongMemEval-V2 2605.12493, MemoryGraft 2512.16962, Memory Poisoning 2601.05504: attack and benchmark papers, no dose curve. (2) 'number of in-context examples distractor fraction nonlinear degradation LLM agent number of wrong exemplars' --recent -> 2605.10828 (the acknowledged neighbour), FALAT 2606.00765, FAMA 2604.25135, 2505.18761: no agent-trace dose study. (3) 'how much memory to retrieve injection budget k ablation agent memory token budget matched control' --recent -> BudgetMem 2602.06025 (query-aware budget-tier routing; a closer learned-budget comparator than MemCon and not cited by the proposal), A-MAC 2603.04549, AURA 2606.02775, Inference-Time Budget Control 2605.05701: none decomposes dose into tokens vs count vs wrong fraction. (4) 'misleading retrieved memory count nonlinear harm tool-use agent length-matched padding control' --recent -> 2607.10608, Memory-Induced Tool-Drift 2605.24941, LongGuard 2608.27580: nothing with length-matched controls on experiential items. (5) 'self-generated in-context examples sequential decision making ALFWorld WebShop trajectory database' -> 2505.00234, TRAD 2403.06221, RA-DT 2410.07071, StraTA 2605.06642. (6) 'how many few-shot trajectories to include agent prompt more examples hurt performance ALFWorld number of demonstrations' -> Skill Blocks 2608.14943, SkillsBench 2602.12670, Skills on the Fly 2605.16986, PANDO 2605.24785: no dose-response curve. Verification: I confirmed by direct lookup every arXiv ID the novelty argument rests on -- 2605.10828 (First Drop of Ink), 2505.00234 (Self-Generated In-Context Examples), 2607.13591 (MemCon), 2605.09330 (Trap of Trajectory/CAMEL), 2608.03297 (Distractor-Aware Truncation), 2510.05381 (Context Length Alone Hurts, EMNLP, 150 cit -- note its title contradicts the proposal's framing of it as merely 'length-alone degradation on static benchmarks'), 2603.07670 (the memory survey, 57 cit), 2605.12978 (Useful Memories Become Faulty), 2603.15666 (Compiled Memory/Atlas), 2607.10608 (The Compliance Trap). The only ID I could not verify is 2609.01556, which the proposal itself already labels unverified and uses only as premise support. Residual risk that abstract-level search cannot close, and which the proposal itself names: a k-ablation table inside 2505.00234 or SEC would partially scoop the raw count curve; neither the proposal nor I checked those appendices.
